mock_call.brief_md:
**What it is:** a recorded role-play of one full first call, you pitching a business. It is never a real business:
you never record a call with a real business. Ask a friend or family member to play the owner, make sure they agree
to be recorded, and give them the owner's sheet below. You don't see the owner's sheet; the engine shows it only to
the person playing the owner (or prints it for you to hand over unread).

**Your scenario:** the engine draws one of the three below and shows you only the "You see" part, the same thing a
Calls card would show you.

**Limits:** **6 minutes at most**, one take, no edits. Audio is enough; video is fine. Send it in from the Learn tab.
A founder listens and either passes it or sends notes and asks for a redo.
must: Say your name and that you're an **independent partner with Station**, give the reason in a few words, and ask if it's a good time.
Ask two or three discovery questions and let the owner talk. Start with what the gap costs them, not the product.
Offer **one** product that fixes the problem they named, said like a name ("Station's Answer collection"), at its **published price**, said once.
Say you **earn a commission**, before you ask for anything.
Handle the worry the owner raises honestly. If you don't know, say Station can confirm it, and don't guess.
Find out **who decides**, and include them.
**Close:** send the page with your link, get an email, and name the **day and time** you'll check back.
Say what happens next without promising a date or doing any of it yourself.

scenarios.title: Dave, HVAC and plumbing
scenarios.you_see_md:
Dave's Heating & Plumbing. HVAC and plumbing, four techs. Best fit: the Answer collection
($297 a month). Why them: calls go to voicemail during the day.
scenarios.owner_sheet_md:
You're 47 and you're under a house most of the day. Last week a
homeowner told you, "I called you first and nobody answered." You don't know how many callers you lose. If asked,
you miss "maybe five or six calls a week" and a job is "a few hundred bucks." Raise one worry: "Will it sound like a
robot?" or "Does it work with Housecall Pro?" Your wife does the books; if asked who decides, say "Me, but I'd show
her." Be busy and a little short at first. Warm up if the partner asks good questions. If they close well, give an
email and agree to a day.

scenarios.title: Rosa and Javier, family taqueria
scenarios.you_see_md:
Rosa's Taqueria & Catering. Family restaurant and catering. Best fit: the Answer collection
($297 a month). Why them: phones ring during the lunch rush.
scenarios.owner_sheet_md:
You and your husband Javier run the taqueria. During the lunch rush
nobody can answer, and last month a catering inquiry went to voicemail and booked someone else. You handle things
online at night; Javier decides about money. Raise the worry: "Do you take online orders?" If the partner pushes you
for a yes, say "I can't, Javier decides." If they ask when both of you can look, say "after 3, when the rush is over."

scenarios.title: Linda, independent realtor
scenarios.you_see_md:
Linda Ortiz Realty. Independent realtor. Best fit: the Follow Up collection ($427 a month). Why them:
1,200 past clients, no follow-up.
scenarios.owner_sheet_md:
You're 57, you've sold houses for 20 years, and you have 1,200 past
clients in a spreadsheet you never contact. New leads wait hours while you're out showing a house. You've seen three
different email products and they all look like a puzzle. Raise the worry: "Is it legal to text my clients?" If the
partner offers to take your spreadsheet, hand it over happily (a good partner refuses).

rubric.label: Says who they are, honestly
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "Hi, it's Sam, an independent partner with Station, calling about missed calls. Did I catch you at a bad time?" Name, independent partner, reason, permission, in the first 15 seconds.
rubric.redo_if: claims to be a Station employee, "calling from Station", "Station's sales team" or an account manager, or hides being a partner.

rubric.label: Discloses the commission
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "I'm paid a commission if you go ahead, so I'll be straight with you." Said plainly, before the close.
rubric.redo_if: the commission is never mentioned, or is mentioned only after the owner has given an email or agreed to buy.

rubric.label: Starts with the gap, lets the owner talk
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "When you're under a house and the phone rings, what happens to that caller?" Two or three questions; the owner talks more than the partner.
rubric.redo_if: pitches a product before asking a single question about the business.

rubric.label: One problem, the smallest fix, said like a name
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "Sounds like the missed calls are the real problem, so let's start there. Station's Answer collection texts back anyone you miss."
rubric.redo_if: leads with a plan or reads out several products before naming the owner's problem, or pitches Radar to a business that doesn't sell to other businesses.

rubric.label: Published price, said once, no deals
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: the live price from station.solutions, said once, with "no contract" and the 14-day free trial only where the product has one.
rubric.redo_if: quotes any price not published on station.solutions, a price for a custom website or hosting & care, a discount, a longer trial, or any share of their commission.

rubric.label: No promises
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "I can't promise a number, because it depends on your business. What I can show you is exactly what it does."
rubric.redo_if: promises a result (jobs, calls, reviews, rankings, money), says "it pays for itself", names a loss figure, gives a go-live date, promises same-day texting, or uses false urgency.

rubric.label: Handles the worry truthfully
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: answers what the guide answers, and says "Station can confirm that, I don't want to guess" for anything else (Housecall Pro, online orders, texting law).
rubric.redo_if: invents a feature, an integration or a compliance answer ("Yes, it works with Housecall Pro", "Yes, you can text all of them", "Callers can't tell it's a robot").

rubric.label: Finds who decides
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "Who else weighs in on something like this? I can send the page to them too."
rubric.redo_if: keeps pushing for a yes after the owner says someone else decides.

rubric.label: Page, email, a dated next step
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "I'll send the page with the price so it's in writing. What's the best email?" Then stops. "I'll check back Thursday at 10. Does that work?" The link is the partner's own.
rubric.redo_if: the call ends with no day and time for the next step, or the partner asks for or accepts card or bank details.

rubric.label: Stays out of the setup and the data
rubric.what_good_sounds_like: "Station emails you the checkout link and receipt, then you book a short onboarding call with your hours and Google link ready."
rubric.redo_if: offers to set anything up, asks for a login or password, or accepts the owner's customer list.
